newsitem.title: USA: US tax bill may not include Amtrak, CBI provisions.
newsitem.headline: US tax bill may not include Amtrak, CBI provisions.

text.p: Last-minute haggling over final details of tax cut legislation would probably result in Amtrak being unable to access new funds in the bill and a Caribbean trade provision not being added in, Senate Republican aides said Wednesday.

The $94 billion five-year net tax cut package includes $2.3 billion in tax credits for the Amtrak rail line, but it will not be available until a comprehensive package of labor and other reforms is approved.

Republicans offered a trade-off to include a provision sought by the White House, called the Caribbean Basin Initiative (CBI), in exchange for including the Amtrak reform package the Republicans want. Senate aides said the White House rejected the Republican Amtrak reform proposal late Tuesday and it appeared neither proposal would be included in the tax bill.
The CBI would allow those countries trade provisions similar to countries in the North American Free Trade Agreement.

The Republicans had made four Amtrak reform proposals, the most controversial of which would require the railroad to negotiate under prevailing labor laws the severance pay and benefits with laid-off workers and would allow Amtrak to contract out work. By law, the rail line is obligated to pay six years severance.
The proposal would also have required a vote by Congress on any liquidation of Amtrak and would have chosen a new board of directors.

Amtrak, as the National Railroad Passenger Corp is commonly known, is an intercity rail service established and partly funded by Congress. It is administered through the U.S Department of Transportation.
Tax writers worked until midnight Tuesday and were still drafting the final bill Wednesday. The legislation was expected to be filed later in the day.
